notes.meaning: Jesus warns his followers not to put on religious displays just to get attention from other people. Doing good deeds is right, but doing them for applause ruins their value before God. When public praise is the goal, God offers no heavenly reward.

Jesus tells his listeners not to show off when they help the poor, like actors playing a role to win human praise. Those who call attention to their charity in public places already have whatever praise they were looking for. That temporary human approval is the only reward they will ever get.

Giving should be done so quietly that it is kept secret even from oneself, without lingering over the deed in pride. The picture of the left hand not knowing what the right hand does means keeping charity as quiet and private as possible. True love focuses on meeting the need rather than patting oneself on the back.

When giving is hidden from the public eye, it honors God as the only audience that matters. The heavenly Father sees everything done in secret and will openly reward sincere kindness. His approval is far more lasting and meaningful than human praise.

Jesus rebukes those who use prayer to make a public show of their holiness. Pretenders chose crowded street corners and busy gathering places at set prayer hours so that crowds would admire them. Human praise is all the reward such showy prayers will ever receive.

Jesus directs his disciples to find a quiet, private room and shut the door to speak with God. This does not forbid praying with others in church, but it protects private prayer from the trap of showing off. God meets the believer in secret and graciously rewards honest communion.

Followers of Jesus must not pile up empty words or repeat chants without thinking, as pagans do. Non-believers often thought their gods could be worn down or persuaded by long, mindless speeches. True prayer is heart-to-heart speech with God, not a magic formula.

Believers do not pray to give God information he lacks, because he already knows every need before a word is spoken. Instead, prayer teaches people to depend on God and readies their hearts to receive his gifts. Disciples can come to him with peaceful confidence rather than nervous chatter.

Jesus provides a model prayer that begins by addressing God as a loving Father in heaven. This shows both close family affection and deep reverence for his holy majesty. The opening request asks that God's name and character be honored and treated as holy everywhere.

This petition asks for God's royal reign of grace and truth to spread throughout the world and in every human heart. It also prays that people on earth will obey God's good purposes as completely and gladly as the angels do in heaven. The believer's highest wish is to see God's rule fully realized.

Jesus teaches his followers to ask God for what is needed to sustain life day by day. This request covers food and daily necessities, reminding believers of their steady dependence on the Lord. Trusting God for today's needs frees his people from anxious worry about tomorrow.

Sins are described here as debts owed to God because of broken laws and neglected duties. The prayer asks God to wipe away that great debt, just as believers pardon people who have wronged them. Asking for mercy while holding onto grudges is contradictory and hardens the heart.

differ.view: Believers are already completely justified and free from eternal punishment, so this petition is about restoring daily family fellowship with God rather than gaining final salvation.
Forgiving others is an active, ongoing condition and measure of God forgiving our sins, so clinging to bitterness limits our experience of his mercy.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: Justification requires ongoing daily repentance, and an unforgiving heart cuts itself off from receiving God's continual mercy.

notes.meaning: Recognizing their own human weakness, believers ask God not to bring them into severe trials that might overwhelm them. They also ask to be rescued from the devil and all moral evil. This request shows a humble desire to stay away from sin and remain safe in God's care.

Jesus underlines the connection between receiving God's forgiveness and offering it to others. When a person readily pardons someone who has caused offense, it proves that the grace of God has truly touched that person's life. A forgiving spirit welcomes the Father's continued mercy.

Refusing to forgive others shuts the door on receiving forgiveness from God. An unforgiving and resentful spirit reveals a heart that has not truly understood its own need for mercy. Anyone who insists on holding grudges cuts themselves off from the Father's pardon.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some older commentators suggested these two verses may have originally been spoken on another occasion, such as after the parable of the unmerciful servant, and placed here by the Gospel writer to explain the prayer.

notes.meaning: Fasting means going without food for a time to focus on God in prayer and humility. Religious posers deliberately looked gloomy and smeared ashes on their faces to make sure everyone saw their sacrifice. Jesus warns that human admiration is the only reward such actors will ever receive.

Jesus instructs his followers to groom themselves normally with washed faces and oiled hair when they fast. By keeping up everyday cleanliness, they avoid drawing attention to their self-denial. True devotion does not put on a show of misery to impress the crowd.

The goal of private fasting is to seek God alone, not to earn a reputation for holiness. The Father sees what is done quietly and will graciously reward genuine devotion. God values secret obedience far above public theater.

Earthly wealth in Bible times often consisted of fine garments, grain, and precious metals. Jesus warns against hoarding worldly riches because clothes get eaten by moths, grain and goods rot, and thieves break through mud-brick walls to steal. Placing ultimate security in temporary things is foolish and dangerous.

Instead of piling up earthly goods, believers are urged to store up treasures in heaven through acts of love, generous giving, and faithful obedience. Heavenly treasures are completely safe from decay and cannot be stolen by any enemy. Living for eternity brings lasting peace and unending security.

A person's deepest loves and thoughts naturally follow whatever they prize most. If wealth on earth is someone's treasure, that person's mind and desires will be trapped in material things. When God and his eternal kingdom are cherished above all else, the heart remains anchored in heaven.

The eye acts as a lamp that lets light into the body to guide every step. In this comparison, a healthy or single eye means having a generous, clear focus on God and his will without mixed motives. A person with this undivided focus has a whole life filled with spiritual light and direction.

A bad eye is cloudy, greedy, or looking in two directions at once, leaving the whole body in darkness. When a person's inner judgment is blinded by selfishness and the love of money, the entire life becomes spiritually dark. That kind of internal darkness is especially terrible because the person thinks they can still see clearly.

A slave cannot give complete, total loyalty to two masters who have opposite interests. Eventually the servant will love one and despise the other, or stay loyal to one and neglect the other. In the same way, no one can be fully devoted to God while serving the god of money.

Jesus urges his disciples not to be consumed by anxious worry about everyday food, drink, and clothing. God has already given the greatest gifts, which are life itself and the human body. Since he provides the greater gift of life, he can certainly be trusted to supply the lesser needs of meals and clothes.

Jesus points to wild birds as an example of God's caring providence. Birds do not farm, harvest, or store grain in barns, yet the heavenly Father keeps them fed. Since human beings are made in God's image and are far more precious to him than birds, he will surely care for them.

Anxious worry is completely useless and cannot change what only God controls. No amount of fretting can add a single hour to a person's lifespan, nor make someone taller. Trusting God accomplishes what stressful worry never could.

Jesus asks why his listeners waste time fretting over clothes, directing them to look at the wild flowers blooming on the hillsides. Wild lilies do not work in the fields or spin thread to make garments. Yet their natural growth shows how effortlessly God provides for his creation.

King Solomon was famous for his great wealth, royal palaces, and splendid royal robes. Yet Jesus explains that even Solomon in his finest court clothing was never as beautifully dressed as a simple wild blossom. God puts richer beauty into common flowers than human royalty can ever produce.

Wild grass and field flowers bloom for only a short time before withering in the summer heat and being burned as fuel in baking ovens. If God dresses such short-lived plants in dazzling splendor, he will surely clothe his own children. Fretting over basic needs reveals weak faith in a caring Father.

Because God takes such good care of the world, disciples must stop fretting over food, drink, and clothing. This repeats the command against anxiety so that fear will not overwhelm the heart. Christians can plan wisely for daily duties without giving in to panic about the future.

People who do not know the true God run frantically after material goods as their highest goal in life. Followers of Christ should not act like unbelievers who think they are completely on their own in the world. The heavenly Father already understands every physical need his children have.

Disciples are told to make God's royal rule and his righteous way of living their top priority. When pleasing God comes first, he promises to provide all the daily necessities of life alongside it. Right priorities put both spiritual duty and material needs in their proper place.

Jesus tells his listeners not to drag tomorrow's possible troubles into today. Tomorrow will have its own concerns, and today already brings enough difficulty and duty to handle. Trusting God one day at a time keeps believers from carrying unnecessary burdens.
